**`vision.yml` no longer configures faces.** `FACE_MODEL` is authoritative for which model produces embeddings and `FACE_RUN` for when it runs; a `face` entry in that file decides neither. A **custom face model configured there is deprecated**: it is still loaded while no embedding model is active, it logs a warning, and its vectors are recorded under the configured model's name rather than its own. Every supported face model needs code that knows its preprocessing contract, so there is nothing useful to configure per installation the way a caption or label model can be.

Run scheduling is `FACE_RUN` (`auto`, `always`, `on-index`, `newly-indexed`, `on-schedule`, `on-demand`, `manual`, `never`). Detection and embedding always run together, so one schedule covers both, and `DISABLE_FACES` turns the whole subsystem off. A `Run` value on a face entry in `vision.yml` is read and **ignored**, with one info-level line naming `FACE_RUN`: two ways to set one schedule raise a precedence question an operator cannot answer from the outside.
**Face detection never sweeps the library on a schedule unless the schedule is named.** Only `on-schedule` and `always` reach the scheduled vision pass; `auto`, `on-demand`, `newly-indexed`, `on-index` and `manual` all stay out of it. Re-examining pictures an earlier pass already saw finds nothing while the detector is unchanged, and it costs a full decode per file - a detector change is what makes another pass worthwhile, and that is a migration or an explicit run. Every schedule other than that sweep is decided by the table `vision.ShouldRunAt` shares with the vision models, so `on-demand` still covers manual and newly indexed work, and `auto` additionally decides between detecting inline and deferring to the pass over newly indexed files, by whether the host is fast enough (`faceEngineRunsOnIndex`).

**`photoprism faces status` is where a stuck instance is diagnosed** (`config` is an alias). It reports the same options as `photoprism config`, named the same way so the two can be read against each other, but grouped as `Global Options`, `Face Detection` and `Face Recognition` and preceded by the state that no value can express: whether faces are being processed, why they are not, and which threshold is holding automatic clustering back. That last one answers the question that otherwise takes hand-written SQL - `Config.faceClusterStatus` counts the unclustered markers against `FACE_CLUSTER_SIZE` and the per-marker score bar separately, so the report names the gate rather than only that clustering did not run, and stays silent when nothing is holding. It connects to a database where `photoprism config` deliberately does not, which is also why the notes under each table can name the model the library actually holds. `face-engine` appears in either report only when it is not `auto`, and `face-detector-path` is blank when detection is off rather than naming weights that will not be loaded.

**Clustering can run twice in one pass, and the second is what reaches a person with four faces.** `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` decides the first pass; `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE_RETRY` repeats it at a lower core **after matching**, so the second pass sees exactly the markers still carrying no `face_id`. That ordering is the whole mechanism and it needs no selection of its own - clustering already reads only unclustered markers, so running it after matching hands it the residue and nothing else. Running it before would let the lower core claim markers an existing cluster was about to take. `facesRunResult.Retried` counts what it added apart from the first pass, since one combined number cannot say whether the option did anything. ⚠ The trigger that decides whether a pass runs at all is evaluated once, for the first pass: it counts markers newer than the newest cluster, so the clusters the first pass just created close it, and re-asking it for the retry would skip the second pass in exactly the runs where the first one did work. Measured on an 89,506-marker library: 625 clusters at a flat core of 5, 942 at a flat core of 4 which *loses* 13 ground-truth markers to fragmentation, and 787 with 5 then 4 - the same ground truth as the baseline, no mixed clusters, and 162 new clusters of which 142 hold three or four samples.

**Two clustering states the report separates.** `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` sets the cluster core and, doubled, the number of new markers that starts an automatic pass (`face.SampleThreshold`, which `Config.Propagate` keeps in step with it). A shortfall there is ordinary and clears itself as indexing continues. The other state does not: a marker older than the newest cluster never counts toward that trigger again, so an instance can hold hundreds of unclustered markers and still look idle. `query.CountFaceClusterGates` therefore counts the unclustered markers twice - once with the recency cut the worker applies and once without - and the status names `photoprism faces update --force` when the two disagree, which is the only thing that clears it.

> Additional merge tuning: set `PHOTOPRISM_FACE_MERGE_MAX_RETRY` to control how often manual clusters are retried (default 1, `0` = unlimited). See the optimizer notes above.

### Breaking Changes

Collected here so they can be turned into release notes rather than rediscovered.

- **SFace ships with `0.72 / 0.70 / 0.25`** (`ClusterDist` / `ClusterRadius` / `MatchDist`), measured against a production library rather than derived from the benchmark harness. The accept distance, `ClusterRadius + MatchDist`, is 0.95. Distances are not comparable across models, so this says nothing about an existing FaceNet library, which keeps `0.64 / 0.42 / 0.4` until `photoprism faces migrate` moves it.
- **`FACE_CLUSTER_SIZE` rises from 60 to 112 and changes unit**, from pixels of the detection thumbnail to pixels of the image the embedding was sampled from (`markers.thumb_size`). The two describe different images, so the old bar landed differently on every original. It is now resolved from the model's own input geometry when unset, so FaceNet compares against 160. A marker with no recorded sample size falls back to the detection size, which is a lower bound on it; `photoprism faces audit` reports how many are in that state and `photoprism faces migrate` fills it. Small faces are still detected, shown and searchable. A library with many small faces will form fewer people than before, and `photoprism faces status` names this bar when it is what holds clustering back.
- **`FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` rises from 4 to 5, and now also moves the clustering trigger.** `face.SampleThreshold` is twice it and was previously frozen at the shipped 8 whatever the option said, so an automatic pass now starts after 10 new markers at the default - and after twice whatever value an instance has set, which for a raised setting means clustering runs **less** often than before.
- **`FACE_EPSILON_DIST` defaults to `0.001`, down from `0.01`, and its ceiling drops from `0.1` to `0.01`.** The ambiguity cutoff is twice the value, so it sits at 0.002 by default and can be raised no further than 0.02. Fewer colliding clusters are retired outright, and the pairs that stop being retired are **not** narrowed in their place: they land below `CollisionDist + Epsilon`, where resolution records a radius that neither `Face.Match` nor candidate selection enforces - the `inert` verdict `photoprism faces conflicts` prints. A cluster already retired stays retired until a person merge clears it. A larger value resolves to the model default with a warning.
- **`--face-skip-children` and `--face-allow-background` are removed**, together with `PHOTOPRISM_FACE_SKIP_CHILDREN` and `PHOTOPRISM_FACE_ALLOW_BACKGROUND`. The environment variables are ignored silently, and both options were `yaml:"-"`, so an `options.yml` carrying them is unaffected. A Compose `command:` line that still passes either **flag** fails to start, because unknown flags are rejected. The flags existed for development rather than for tuning a library.
- **The out-of-distribution background filter is gone**, and it was enabled by default (`IgnoreBackground` defaulted to true) for every existing FaceNet library. Removing it is required rather than optional: it compared each embedding against bundled FaceNet-space reference vectors, so under any model of a different width every face would have been classified as background and matching would have stopped library-wide. The child filter it is paired with was already inert. Measured under FaceNet with both forced on, neither fired.
- **A custom face model in `vision.yml` is deprecated** in favor of `FACE_MODEL` — see § Configuration Summary. It still works and warns.
- **`FACE_MODEL` defaults to unset and is written once it has been detected.** `auto` is the spelling the help offers, and an unsupported value is reported and applies as if nothing were set, without its detected name being written down. Changing the model afterwards is `photoprism faces migrate`, which updates `options.yml` itself; an environment variable no longer changes the model of a library that already has one. `photoprism reset` clears the pin, because a reset leaves no vectors for it to keep comparable.
- **A recognition run names an unnamed cluster whose recognized faces agree on one person.** A single automatic or XMP name still never names its cluster. When at least `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` faces name the same person - automatically, or from an XMP sidecar naming a person who is marked as Verified or was named by hand on a valid face marker - they are at least half of the cluster's valid faces, and no face in it carries a name a person gave, the cluster and its unnamed faces are named after that person and it leaves People > New. The name stays automatic, so a default `faces reset` removes it, and naming one face by hand relabels no other face. A face named after another person than its cluster is reported to the cluster as a collision, which narrows it - releasing its automatic faces beyond the new radius to be matched again - or marks it ambiguous, and the face itself moves to a face of its new person where it can seed one, or otherwise waits for matching. `faces audit` reports how many clusters qualify.
- **Removing a face's name keeps it unnamed.** Matching may still group the face with others, but does not assign a person to a face whose name a person removed, even in a forced run; only a face-model migration that re-embeds it from another model lets it be recognized again. During a recognition run, a face whose XMP name lost its person is linked only to a person who still exists, and never names its cluster.
- **A library the configured model cannot read pauses embedding work instead of filtering it.** Generation, clustering and matching stop after one warning until `photoprism faces migrate` reconciles them. Detection pauses with it, since a face is only saved with its embedding.
- **The InsightFace models are absent from the `--face-model` help and refused unless their terms are accepted.** Their installers moved to `scripts/dist/`, so they ship in published images; the weights are still never bundled.
- **Face detection stays out of the scheduled vision pass unless the schedule is named.** Only `FACE_RUN=on-schedule` and `always` sweep the library. `on-demand` covers manual and newly indexed work but no longer re-examines pictures an earlier pass already saw, which found nothing while the detector was unchanged and cost a full decode per file.
- **`detect` is no longer accepted for `FACE_DETECTOR` or `FACE_MODEL`.** It was an accepted spelling of `auto` during development and never shipped. A value still set reads as unknown: reported once, then applied as a request to derive one. `FACE_MODEL=detect` additionally stops the detected name being recorded, so correct it in `options.yml` to avoid re-detecting on every start.
- **`photoprism faces migrate` exits non-zero whenever a marker lost its vector**, not only when a clusterable one did. The ratio guard still refuses a finalize on clusterable loss alone, but a run that discarded a third of a library below the clustering bars used to be indistinguishable from a clean one to anything checking the exit status. Automation that treated `0` as "nothing lost" needs revisiting.
- **A migration now rewrites `score` and `size` on every re-detected marker**, alongside `detect_model` and `landmarks_json`. The clustering bars are looked up by `detect_model`, so a marker relabeled with the new detector while keeping the old one's score was judged at a calibration it was never scored against.
- **`photoprism faces status` replaces the flat `faces config` table.** Rows are named by option, grouped as `Global Options` / `Face Detection` / `Face Recognition`, and the state is prose above them. `config` is an alias; there are no longer `Enabled`, `Vision Config` or `Locked` rows.
- **A marker between two clusters that name two different people is now left unassigned**, where it previously went to whichever was marginally closer, and an assignment an earlier run made on that coin toss is cleared. A cluster carrying no name is not a rival in either direction, so a fragmented library is barely affected - except for a marker that already carries a hand-set name, which is held to the stricter test, because there an unnamed winner would mint an identity rather than pick a cluster. Such a marker never has its existing subject withdrawn. `FACE_MATCH_MARGIN=-1` restores the old behavior.
- **Hand-labeled faces merge at what a cluster may accept rather than at the link distance.** `Face.Mergeable` now admits a pair up to `ClusterRadius + MatchDist` (0.95 on SFace) instead of `ClusterDist` (0.72). Two faces of one person sit further apart than the link distance more often than not - measured over 7,485 same-person marker pairs on a development library, the median is 0.985 and only 2.2 % fall inside 0.72 - so single-face clusters a person named by hand waited indefinitely, and one subject there held twelve with no pair inside the old bound. `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` is unaffected; this is the manual path only, where a person has already asserted the identity and no cluster is being discovered. Existing single-face clusters merge on the next `photoprism faces optimize` once a subject has `face.ManualClusterCore` (3) of them within the wider bound, so expect a one-off round of merges on an upgraded library.
- **Clustering no longer depends on the order the markers arrive in.** `alg.DBSCAN` forms clusters from the connected components of the core faces and attaches every remaining face afterwards, only where the cores around it agree on a single cluster; one that two clusters can both reach stays unclustered. The expansion this replaced took a face into whichever cluster reached it first and never reconsidered one it had already passed over, so re-indexing the same library in a different order put a measured 327 of 11,738 clustered faces under a different cluster. `FACE_CLUSTER_CORE` still bars what may *form* a cluster rather than flooring how large one ends up, so a result below it stays possible - much rarer than before. Existing clusters are untouched until `photoprism faces update --force` or a soft `photoprism faces reset` re-forms them.
- **A cluster wider than what it accepts is re-clustered rather than created.** DBSCAN bounds the link distance rather than the width of the result, so a library where faces chain gets more, narrower clusters instead of one that holds several people. A subject may own several clusters by design - `faces.subj_uid` is a plain index, and a curated library already holds three for one person - so this makes an existing condition more common rather than a new one. `Faces.Optimize` does not repair it: it merges only the clusters a person created by hand (`query.ManuallyAddedFaces` filters `face_src = manual`), so a fragmented person is named per cluster. The check runs where a cluster is created, so one an earlier release already stored keeps its shape until `photoprism faces update --force` re-clusters the markers it does not hold, or a soft `photoprism faces reset` followed by `photoprism faces update` re-forms it outright.
- **`FACE_COLLISION_DIST` is the same for every model**, at `0.05`, rather than scaled with the model's distance scale. On SFace the first collision distance that narrows a cluster moves from 0.071 to 0.051, so marginally more clusters are narrowed by a recorded collision. It is also the floor `Config.faceThreshold` holds the three configurable distances above, so the range an operator may set widens by the same amount - most for ArcFace R50, whose floor moves from 0.084.
- **A person's cover is the largest and most confident face among their valid markers**, with a marker whose subject automatic clustering did not assign taken first, rather than by the stored `markers.q` score. Every source other than automatic clustering shares that one rank, so size decides between them: a larger face named from an XMP sidecar outranks a smaller one a person typed. Covers change on the next refresh for people whose stored score no longer described their markers, and MariaDB and SQLite now pick the same one; on SQLite a rejected or non-face marker can no longer become a cover at all. A cover set by hand is left alone, and any marker can be pinned as one from **Set as Cover Image** in the Edit dialog's People tab.
- **A face crop is drawn from a rendition wide enough to supply it**, measured rather than taken from the size in its filename. A fit rendition reaches that size only on its longer edge, so the file named `1920x1200` holds a 4:3 picture 1600 px wide and a 3:4 one 900 px wide. Faces in tall pictures were the ones most often stretched onto the template, and their embeddings change accordingly; `photoprism faces migrate` re-embeds a library that should be consistent throughout.
- **A marker placed without a detector records its size the way a detected one does**, in pixels of the `Fit720` detection thumbnail. A face marker drawn in the app and one imported from an XMP region are now comparable with detected markers, where they used to be measured against the original and against a fixed nominal size. Neither kind carries an embedding, so this reaches cover selection, the faces search and the `photoprism faces status` counters rather than clustering.
- **`Q` is gone from the marker API payload.** `entity.Marker` no longer carries it, so the marker endpoints return one field fewer; the web UI never read it. `markers.q` is no longer written or read: an existing database keeps the column until a migration drops it, and a new install never creates it, since the schema follows the struct.

# FindTrace — Missing Person Intelligence System

A browser-based AI system for real-time face detection, recognition, and age progression to help locate missing persons. Built entirely as a **single HTML file** with zero server infrastructure.

**📄 IEEE Research Paper Published** — *"Child Facial Age Progression and Regression for Missing Children"*

## Features

- **Real-Time Face Detection** — TinyFaceDetector running at 8–12 FPS via TensorFlow.js
- **Face Recognition** — 128-dimensional face embeddings with Euclidean distance matching (< 5ms per match)
- **Age Progression/Regression** — Canvas-based 7-stage aging pipeline (200–500ms processing)
- **GPS Location Tracking** — Browser Geolocation API with Google Maps integration
- **Case Management** — Register missing persons with 12+ physical descriptors
- **Automated Reports** — Generate self-contained HTML reports with embedded images
- **100% Client-Side** — Zero data leaves the browser, fully privacy-preserving

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| AI/ML | TensorFlow.js, face-api.js |
| Detection | TinyFaceDetector (TinyYOLOv2) |
| Recognition | FaceRecognitionNet (ResNet, 128-D) |
| Frontend | HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ES6+ |
| Maps | Google Maps API |
| Storage | Browser localStorage |

## How to Run

Just open `index.html` in Chrome or Edge. That's it — no installation needed.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/raigaurav26/FindTrace.git
cd FindTrace
start index.html
```

Allow camera access when prompted.

## How It Works

### 1. Case Registration
Users register a missing person case by uploading a photo and entering details like name, age, physical descriptors (skin tone, face shape, hair color, distinguishing marks). The system extracts a **128-dimensional face descriptor** from the uploaded photo and stores it in browser localStorage.

### 2. Real-Time Face Detection
The system accesses the device webcam and runs **TinyFaceDetector** (a TinyYOLOv2-based model) on each video frame at 8–12 FPS. It detects faces using a 416×416 pixel input with a score threshold of 0.4 and Non-Maximum Suppression (IoU = 0.5).

### 3. Face Recognition & Matching
For each detected face, the pipeline:
1. Extracts **68 facial landmarks** using FaceLandmark68Net
2. Generates a **128-D face descriptor** using FaceRecognitionNet (ResNet-based)
3. Computes **Euclidean distance** against all stored reference descriptors
4. Declares a match when distance < 0.55 (configurable threshold)
5. Calculates confidence: `Confidence = max(0, 1 - distance/threshold) × 100%`

A 100-frame cooldown prevents duplicate alerts.

### 4. Age Progression Engine
The canvas-based pipeline applies 7 procedural aging effects scaled by an exponential curve:
1. Pixel-level desaturation
2. Wrinkle generation at anatomical positions
3. Hair greying
4. Under-eye and temple hollowing
5. Jawline sagging
6. Skin texture deterioration
7. Cheek hollowing

Processing time: 200–500ms without any GPU server.

### 5. Age Regression Engine
Reverses aging effects by increasing skin saturation, applying Gaussian blur, increasing brightness, and reducing contrast.

### 6. GPS & Location Intelligence
Upon a match detection, the system captures GPS coordinates using the Browser Geolocation API (high-accuracy mode) with IP-based fallback via ipapi.co, generating clickable Google Maps links.

### 7. Automated Report Generation
Generates self-contained HTML reports with base64-embedded images, subject profiles, physical descriptors, and chronological match event logs with GPS coordinates.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             Presentation Layer                   │
│        Three-panel responsive dashboard          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            Application Modules                   │
│  Case Mgmt │ Detection │ Age Engine │ GPS │ Reports │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            AI/ML Processing                      │
│     face-api.js + TensorFlow.js (WebGL)          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            Data Persistence                      │
│       Browser localStorage (JSON)                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            External Services                     │
│   Geolocation API │ Google Maps │ CDN Models     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Performance

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Detection Latency | 80–150ms/frame |
| Descriptor Extraction | 50–100ms/face |
| Face Matching | < 5ms |
| Age Progression | 200–500ms |
| Frame Rate | 8–12 FPS |
| Report Generation | < 100ms |
| Page Load | 2–4 seconds |

| Browser | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Chrome | ✅ Full support (best performance) |
